messages.subject: Questions about communities
messages.body_plain:
Dear Christopher Watson,

I am a user of this very great toolbox. For the moment I only use it for communities detection and have few questions for you :

1. Is it possible to have a more "exploded" view of the nodes and communities ? Because I have 164 nodes and it is very hard to analyse it (i joined an example of my results to better understand). I tested different types of layout but any gave me satisfaction..

2. What are the difference between the color of the node, and the color of the "groups" in the layout ? I think that the color node is for the community, but if 2 nodes with different color and any connection between them are grouped, does it mean that they are not in the same community but can participate in a same organization ?

I thank you in advance for your answers.

Clément Bournonville

messages.subject: Re: [brainGraph-help] Questions about communities
messages.body_plain:
Hi Clement,
Thank you for your kind words. I hope it is useful to you.

Both of your questions are actually specific to igraph, but I will try:
1. I don't think there is a way to tweak the parameters of the Fruchterman-Reingold method so that the vertices won't be placed as close together. You might have more luck using "Gephi". If your desired graph is in an object called "myGraph", you can use the command
write.graph(myGraph, format='graphml', file='myGraph.graphml')

2. The vertices are indeed colored based on community membership. I believe the edge coloring has meaning, as well: red edges are *inter*-modular, whereas gray edges are *intra*-modular. To view without the colored shapes surrounding vertices, you can pass the argument "mark.groups=NULL". The problem with multiple vertices appearing to fall within multiple of those "boxes" is simply a problem inherent to 2-dimensional plotting of graphs. There will be some overlap necessarily.

If you would like to see the communities in the spatial layout of the brain, you can do so easily, using something like:
plot_brainGraph_mni('axial')
plot_brainGraph(g[[1]][[N]], vertex.label=NA, vertex.size=5, vertex.color=V(g[[1]][[N]])$color.comm, edge.width=0)

This will not show the edges, so you can more easily see the vertices' and their community memberships.

Let me know if you have more questions,
Chris

Chris

messages.body_plain:

I have made a minor update to v0.54.0. It is available via Github. I have added 2 functions to perform the analyses that are in Saggar et al. 2015 <http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1053811915006151>.

I have also updated the User Guide to reflect these minor changes. Chapter 5.11 is new and reflects the new functions.

Chris

messages.subject: Update to v0.55.0
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I have made a minor update to v0.55.0. This will likely be a new accepted version on CRAN; so you can (in a day or 2) install in R simply by "install.packages('brainGraph')". It is also available via Github, as usual.

I added a function, "plot_rich_norm", that simplifies plotting the rich-club coefficient curves. For all changes, please see the "NEWS.md" file (highlighted in green) at the Github diff page <https://github.com/cwatson/brainGraph/commit/4740ea634b0aa532548bce047e1dfd50cf94b4b3?short_path=8312ad0#diff-8312ad0561ef661716b48d09478362f3>.

I have also updated the User Guide to reflect these minor changes.

Happy Holidays!
Chris

messages.subject: Update to v0.56.0
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I have made a minor update to v0.56.0 (with one "major" change).

brainGraph now requires the package "RcppEigen"; this allows for very fast linear model calculations. The function "group.graph.diffs" (equivalent to a voxel-wise analysis in SPM/FSL/etc.) has been updated accordingly. For all changes, please see the "NEWS.md" file (highlighted in green) at the Github diff page <https://github.com/cwatson/brainGraph/commit/fe08816bec38c95412cdb5429b2a1414ea3116bf?short_path=8312ad0#diff-8312ad0561ef661716b48d09478362f3>.

The User Guide will be updated very soon to reflect these changes.

Chris

messages.subject: Update to v0.57.0
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I have made a minor update to v0.57.0 (with one "major" addition).

I have finally implemented the network-based statistic, via the function "NBS"! You will now have to install the package "permute" to generate a set of random permutations. I also added a function to calculate mean edge distances per vertex. For all changes, please see the "NEWS.md" file (highlighted in green) at the Github diff page <https://github.com/cwatson/brainGraph/commit/ec1ee8500601fd7e856dbb9b19ee01dd3de09bf5?short_path=8312ad0#diff-8312ad0561ef661716b48d09478362f3>.

The User Guide has been updated as well.

Happy New Year!
Chris
